rationale:
DECISION. Split root.deformation-a1.onto_skeleton-a1 (deformation_onto_skeleton) into 11 children: 4 new theorems and 7 comparator-accepted declarations reused by name with byte-identical frozen types. Without the split, the Lean proof of this node would have to contain the whole theory of products, smooth and Lipschitz push-forwards and homotopies of normal currents (Simon 2.17–2.29, 3.2(2)). The pinned project has none of it: SimonGMT has only affine push-forwards (Chapter06/AffineCurrentPushforward.lean), Mathlib has no currents, and the in-flight DAG nodes on products (iwl_cr_interval_product_im) and smooth push-forwards (iwl_smooth_pushforward) are unaccepted, cover only integer-multiplicity currents, and are reserved by another branch. That theory is the parent's Part I. It is a genuine, reusable obligation and the main formalization risk, so it becomes one child with a clean operator interface. The M-limit lemma, the Chebyshev radius selection and the closedness of the skeleton are further self-contained obligations. Steps 1–8 of the supplied proof stay in the parent as assembly.

CHILDREN ↔ SUPPLIED PROOF.
- pushforward_homotopy (deformation_pushforward_homotopy, new): Part I of the supplied proof, i.e. A2(a)–(e) (2.17–2.29), A4(a),(d) (3.2(2)), I.6 and I.7, packaged as operators P_k (push-forward by f) and H_k (push-forward of [[(0,1)]]×X by the straight-line homotopy from f to the identity). They come with masses (1)–(2), supports (3)–(4), integrality (5), linearity (7), boundary commutation (8) and the homotopy formula (9), plus the analytic core of Step 7 (6). The premise is (S5′), the exact conclusion of the declared sibling deformation_im_pushforward_limit after its premise LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity. The parent discharges it with deformation_im_pushforward_limit hLp; a scratch elaboration of `hA (hS5 hLp)` type-checks. The child is stated for one map f near arbitrary closed regions E on which f is Lipschitz. This replaces the parent's σ-dependent McShane extensions ψ̄_σ, h̄_σ: the operators depend only on f, and their independence of the region is proved inside the child (6.2), as I.6 proves independence of σ. The homotopy runs from f (t = 0) to the identity (t = 1), so (9) reads X − P X = ∂H X + H ∂X, the corrected sign of erratum (iii); R and S then need no sign change.
- telescope_limit (deformation_telescope_limit, new): I.5 (printed (19)), in the summable-increment form in which Steps 4–6 use it. It gives weak convergence, the mass bound (24), the tail bound M(A′ − A_ν) ≤ Σ_{μ≥ν} M(B_μ) (the hypothesis of the sibling deformation_im_completeness) and support preservation.
- good_radius (deformation_good_radius, new): the Chebyshev selection of σ_ν in Step 2 (printed (10)).
- skeleton_closed (deformation_skeleton_isClosed, new): closedness of L_n = ⋃_F latticeFace 1 F, used in Step 6 ((22)); proved for every ρ > 0.
- mass_bound (cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le), vanish_off_support (isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support), support_lemmas (iwl_cr_support_lemmas; depends on vanish_off_support exactly as in its own branch): reused accepted facts (F1)–(F3), the parent's (S3)(e) and the support steps of I.5, I.6 and Step 6.
- support_null (lpf_rectifiable_support_null, with its own dependency simple_nvector_algebra = lpf_simple_nvector_algebra) and lipschitz_area (lpf_raf_local_lipschitz_area, the area formula with multiplicities, with its own dependency fiber_sum_glue = lpf_raf_fiber_sum_glue): reused accepted facts (F9), (F10) of pushforward_homotopy. support_null is the bracket of I.7 (H^k(M ∖ spt X) = 0). lipschitz_area is the area formula behind A4(d)'s product formula H^{k+1}⌞((0,1)×M) = L¹ × H^k⌞M. It is used with weights 1/multiplicity on bounded pieces, so no injective decomposition is needed.

ASSEMBLY (the selected statement from the children, the declared siblings (S1)–(S5) and the premises (Sl), (Lp), by the supplied proof). Fix m, ℓ ≥ 1, D := m + 1 + ℓ, n := m + 1. Take c_A from deformation_retraction, c_B from deformation_good_center and c = c(D, ·) from pushforward_homotopy applied to (S5′) = deformation_im_pushforward_limit hLp; all depend only on (m, ℓ). Fix T with M(T) + M(∂T) < ∞.
 Step 1: (S3) for T and ∂T gives μ_T, μ_∂. (S2) gives a with μ({d_a < σ}) ≤ c_Bσ^{n+1}μ(ℝ^D) for σ ∈ (0, 1/4). (S1) gives ψ. Put La as in (S1), d_a := infDist · La (1-Lipschitz, so ‖Dd_a‖ ≤ 1 everywhere), E_σ := {x | σ ≤ d_a(x)} (closed, disjoint from La).
 Step 2: (Sl) for T (and for ∂T when m ≥ 1) with f = d_a, L = L_W = 1, W = univ. Slices are identified by the uniqueness clause of (S3): ∂T_t = (∂T)_t + S_t and ∂S_t = −S′_t. On (2^{−ν−1}, 2^{−ν}), good_radius with the slicing majorant g, K := M(T⌞{2^{−ν−1} < d_a < 2^{−ν}}) ≤ c_B2^{−ν(n+1)}M(T), and N := Ioo(2^{−ν−1}, 2^{−ν}) ∩ {g′ = ∞} when m ≥ 1 (null, since ∫ g′ < ∞; g′ the majorant for ∂T), resp. N := ∅ when m = 0, gives σ_ν with M(S_{σ_ν}) ≤ 4c_B2^{−νn}M(T) and M(S′_{σ_ν}) ≤ g′(σ_ν) < ∞. The printed extra requirement that S_{σ_ν} be integer multiplicity can be added to N when T is integer multiplicity (null set by (Sl)). It is not needed, because the integrality of Q, R, S comes from the pieces in Step 5. The pieces X_ν, Z′_ν, Y_ν, Z_ν and their identities, masses and supports follow from (S3) exactly as printed.
 Step 3: apply pushforward_homotopy to f := ψ with data (E_σ, Λ := c_A/(σ/2), δ := σ/2, b := √D). Lipschitz: thickening (σ/2) E_σ ⊆ {σ/2 ≤ d_a}, where ψ is (c_A/(σ/2))-Lipschitz by (S1)(iii), since σ/2 ≤ 1/4. Displacement: |ψ(x) − x| ≤ √D off La by (S1)(ii), taking z := ⌊x⌋. Every piece is normal: ∂X_ν = Z′_ν − S_{σ_ν}, and for m ≥ 1, ∂Z′_ν = −S′_{σ_ν}, ∂Z_ν = S′_{σ_ν} − S′_{σ_{ν+1}}, ∂S_{σ_ν} = −S′_{σ_ν}. For m = 0 the HEq condition is vacuous. Clauses (1)–(2) with σ = σ_{ν+1} (Λ ≤ 8c_A2^ν), resp. σ_ν, give (11)–(16) and the initial bounds at ν = 3.
 Step 4: linearity (7) gives P X_{ν+1} = P X_ν + P Y_ν, H X_{ν+1} = H X_ν + H Y_ν, P Z′_{ν+1} = P Z′_ν + P Z_ν, H Z′_{ν+1} = H Z′_ν + H Z_ν, with common data E_{σ_{ν+1}}. Then telescope_limit gives Q := lim P_n X_ν, R := lim H_n X_ν and S := lim H_m Z′_ν (the sums of (11)–(14) are finite). Clause (9) plus (7) (∂X_ν = Z′_ν − S_{σ_ν}, common data E_{σ_ν}) give X_ν − P X_ν = ∂H X_ν + H Z′_ν − H S_{σ_ν}. Evaluate on ω and let ν → ∞. By mass_bound, T(ω) − X_ν(ω) → 0 (M(T⌞{d_a < σ_ν}) → 0) and H S_{σ_ν}(ω) → 0 (by (16)). Hence T(ω) − Q(ω) = ∂R(ω) + S(ω), which is (21).
 Step 5: by (S3), X_ν (resp. Z′_ν) is integer multiplicity if T (resp. ∂T) is. Clause (5) makes P X_ν, H X_ν, H Z′_ν integer multiplicity. The tail bound of telescope_limit with ENNReal.tendsto_sum_nat_add is the hypothesis of (S4) deformation_im_completeness, so Q, R and S are integer multiplicity.
 Step 6: (3) and (S1)(i) give spt P X_ν ⊆ closure ψ(spt X_ν) ⊆ L_n, since L_n is closed (skeleton_closed). (3), (4) with b = √D give spt P X_ν, spt H X_ν ⊆ cthickening √D (spt T) and spt H Z′_ν, spt P Z′_ν ⊆ cthickening √D (spt ∂T). The support clause of telescope_limit then gives (22)–(23) with closed thickenings (erratum (v)); the support of ∂Q is treated with (25) below. Masses: (24) from the mass clause of telescope_limit. For (25) and spt ∂Q, apply telescope_limit a fourth time, to A″_ν := P_m Z′_{ν+3} with increments P_m Z_{ν+3} (summable by (12)). This gives Q′ with M(Q′) ≤ M(P Z′_3) + Σ M(P Z_ν) ≤ cM(∂T) and spt Q′ ⊆ cthickening √D (spt ∂T). Since ∂Q(ω) = Q(dω) = lim P X_ν(dω) = lim (P Z′_ν(ω) − P S_{σ_ν}(ω)) (clauses (8), (7)) and |P S_{σ_ν}(ω)| ≤ M(P S_{σ_ν})‖ω‖ → 0 (mass_bound, (15)), we get ∂Q = Q′ by ext. Hence M(∂Q) ≤ cM(∂T) and spt ∂Q = spt Q′ ⊆ cthickening √D (spt ∂T). Where masses of pointwise linear combinations are bounded (normality of ∂X_ν, ∂Y_ν, ∂Z_ν; M(X₂) in (7)), the bound M(aY₁ + bY₂) ≤ |a|M(Y₁) + |b|M(Y₂) is the routine sSup argument with mass_bound.
 Step 7: given F, ball y r with ball ∩ L_n ⊆ latticeFace 1 F and ω as in the statement, take δ₀ > 0 with thickening δ₀ (tsupport ω) ⊆ ball y r (IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open). Apply (6) to X_ν with α := F.2, z_i := F.1 i and ε := min(σ_ν/2, δ₀). If x ∈ thickening ε (spt X_ν) then d_a(x) > σ_ν/2 > 0, so x ∉ La and ψ(x) ∈ L_n by (S1)(i). If moreover ψ(x) ∈ thickening ε (tsupport ω), then ψ(x) ∈ ball y r ∩ L_n ⊆ latticeFace 1 F, so ψ(x)_i = F.1 i for i ∉ range F.2. Hence P X_ν(ω) = 0 for all ν and Q(ω) = 0.
 Step 8: R : D_{m+2} matches H_{m+1} (degree m + 1 + 1 = m + 2 by rfl, checked in Lean); S, Q : D_{m+1}. C := the maximum of the explicit constants, depending only on (m, ℓ).

subproblems.title: Currents annihilate test forms supported off their support
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and every test form ω ∈ TestFormOn U n (C^∞, compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ U): if tsupport ω is disjoint from spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T) (zeroRegion(T) = union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T(η) = 0 for every test form η with tsupport η ⊆ W), then T(ω) = 0.

Source: the parenthetical argument in Step 1 of the parent proof ("a test form supported in the open zero region is annihilated: cover its compact support by finitely many open sets on which T vanishes and use a partition of unity"), with Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T), written out for the exact SimonGMT definitions.

Notation. For T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, `T.VanishesOn W` means T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ W. Let 𝒲 be the family of all W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W. By definition T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲 and T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion.

1. Let K := tsupport ω. Since ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, ω is C^∞, has compact support (so K is compact, in particular closed) and K ⊆ U.
2. K ⊆ ⋃𝒲. Let x ∈ K. Then x ∈ U, and x ∉ T.support by the disjointness hypothesis, i.e. x ∉ U ∖ T.zeroRegion; hence x ∈ T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲.
3. Every member of 𝒲 is open, so by compactness of K there are finitely many W_1, …, W_r ∈ 𝒲 (r ≥ 0; r = 0 when K = ∅) with K ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_r (e.g. `IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover_image`; it is convenient to index the cover by the resulting finite subfamily rather than by Fin r).
4. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with the model with corners 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), is a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, σ-compact smooth manifold, and K is closed and covered by the open sets W_i (i ranging over the finite index set of step 3). Hence there is a smooth partition of unity on K subordinate to (W_i): C^∞ functions ψ_1, …, ψ_r : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_i ψ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K (Mathlib `SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`; a real-valued `ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) 𝓘(ℝ)` function of class C^∞ is `ContDiff ℝ ∞` by `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`).
5. For each i put η_i(x) := ψ_i(x) • ω(x). Then η_i is C^∞ (a C^∞ scalar function times a C^∞ form). If ω(x) = 0 or ψ_i(x) = 0 then η_i(x) = 0, so support η_i ⊆ support ω ∩ support ψ_i; taking closures, tsupport η_i ⊆ K ∩ tsupport ψ_i ⊆ U ∩ W_i. In particular η_i has compact support (closed subset of the compact K). Thus η_i ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport η_i ⊆ W_i.
6. Since W_i ∈ 𝒲, T vanishes on W_i, so T(η_i) = 0 for every i.
7. ω = Σ_i η_i in TestFormOn U n (checked pointwise). If x ∈ K, then Σ_i ψ_i(x) • ω(x) = (Σ_i ψ_i(x)) • ω(x) = ω(x). If x ∉ K, then x ∉ support ω, so ω(x) = 0 and every η_i(x) = 0. (If r = 0 then K = ∅, ω = 0 and both sides are 0.)
8. T acts ℝ-linearly on TestFormOn U n (T.toCurrent is a linear map), so by steps 6 and 7, T(ω) = Σ_i T(η_i) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U disjoint from spt T, hence contained in the zero region, i.e. covered by the open sets W on which T vanishes.
Extract a finite subcover W_1, …, W_r of tsupport ω.
Take a smooth partition of unity ψ_1, …, ψ_r on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i (Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate).
Each ψ_i • ω is a test form in U with tsupport in W_i, so T(ψ_i • ω) = 0.
ω = Σ_i ψ_i • ω pointwise, so T(ω) = 0 by linearity.

Source: parent proof Step 2 (basic mass estimate). It is stated with an explicit real bound B for M_W(T) and an explicit pointwise bound C for |ω|, which avoids dividing by sup|ω| and any case distinction on ω = 0.

Notation: for an n-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P, I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ψ)) over ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W = {ψ ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ψ ⊆ W and |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}.

1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and a covector α, |tα| = |t|·|α|. Each coefficient satisfies (tα)(e_I) = t·α(e_I), so the sum of squares is multiplied by t², and √(t²S) = |t|·√S.
2. (C ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ C.
3. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix a real c > C, so c > 0. Let s ∈ {c⁻¹, −c⁻¹}. TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, so s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

Throughout, G(v) := (⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is the Gram matrix of v = (v₁,…,v_n) and, for a real n×n matrix B and τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n), (Bτ)_i := Σ_j B_ij τ_j. This is item (P1) of the parent proof.

1. (Second identity: change of frame.) Let α be any n-covector. By multilinearity,
 α(Bτ) = Σ_{g : Fin n → Fin n} (Π_i B_{i g(i)}) · α(τ_{g(1)}, …, τ_{g(n)}).
 If g is not injective two arguments coincide and the term vanishes because α is alternating. If g = σ is a permutation, α(τ∘σ) = sign(σ) α(τ). Hence α(Bτ) = (Σ_σ sign(σ) Π_i B_{iσ(i)}) α(τ) = det(B) α(τ) by the Leibniz formula (det B = det Bᵀ, so the row/column convention is immaterial). As this holds for every α, simpleNVector(Bτ) = det(B) • simpleNVector τ. For n = 0 both sides are the functional α ↦ α(∅) and the determinant of the empty matrix is 1.

2. (Gram matrices transform by congruence.) G(Bτ)_{ik} = ⟨Σ_j B_ij τ_j, Σ_l B_kl τ_l⟩ = (B G(τ) Bᵀ)_{ik}; hence det G(Bτ) = det(B)² det G(τ).

3. (Upper bound for orthonormal families.) If τ is orthonormal then |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|τ_i| = ‖α‖ for every α, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ 1.

4. (Lower bound for orthonormal families.) Let τ be orthonormal (n ≥ 1), W := span τ and π_W the orthogonal projection onto W. Define α₀(u₁,…,u_n) := det(⟨u_i, τ_j⟩)_{i,j}. It is n-linear and alternating (a determinant whose i-th row depends linearly on u_i, and two equal u's give two equal rows) and continuous (finite dimension). The i-th row (⟨u_i,τ_j⟩)_j is the coordinate vector of π_W u_i in the orthonormal basis τ, of Euclidean length |π_W u_i| ≤ |u_i|. By Hadamard's inequality |det A| ≤ Π_i |row_i(A)| (proof: if the rows are dependent det A = 0; otherwise Gram–Schmidt on the rows gives A = R O with O orthogonal and R lower triangular with diagonal entries |a_i^⊥| ≤ |a_i|, a_i^⊥ the component of the i-th row orthogonal to the previous rows, so |det A| = Π|a_i^⊥| ≤ Π|a_i|; in Lean this is `Orientation.abs_volumeForm_apply_le` for the volume form of W composed with π_W) we get |α₀(u)| ≤ Π|u_i|, i.e. ‖α₀‖ ≤ 1. Since α₀(τ) = det(⟨τ_i,τ_j⟩) = det I = 1, ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≥ |simpleNVector τ (α₀)| / ‖α₀‖ ≥ 1. Together with step 3: ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1 = det G(τ). For n = 0, 0-covectors are the constants c = α(∅) with ‖α‖ = |c|, so ‖simpleNVector ∅‖ = 1 = det of the empty matrix.

5. (Dependent families.) If v₁,…,v_n are linearly dependent then α(v) = 0 for every alternating α (`AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent`), so simpleNVector v = 0 and ‖simpleNVector v‖² = 0. Also G(v) is singular: for a nontrivial c with Σ_j c_j v_j = 0 we get G(v)c = (⟨v_i, Σ_j c_j v_j⟩)_i = 0, so det G(v) = 0. The first identity holds. (This covers in particular n > P.)

6. (Independent families.) If v is linearly independent, Gram–Schmidt produces an orthonormal τ with span τ = span v and v = Bτ, B_ij = ⟨v_i, τ_j⟩, B invertible. By step 1, simpleNVector v = det(B) • simpleNVector τ, so by step 4, ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |det B|. By step 2 and G(τ) = I, det G(v) = det(B)². Hence ‖simpleNVector v‖² = det G(v) = det (Matrix.of fun i j => ⟨v_i, v_j⟩).

Steps 5–6 give the first conjunct for every v; step 1 gives the second conjunct. ∎

Gram matrices transform by congruence: det G(Bτ) = det(B)²·det G(τ).
For orthonormal τ: ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ Π|τ_i| = 1, and the covector det(⟨u_i,τ_j⟩) has norm ≤ 1 by Hadamard and value 1 at τ, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1.
Dependent families: simpleNVector v = 0 and det G(v) = 0.
Independent families: Gram–Schmidt v = Bτ gives ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |det B| and det G(v) = det(B)².

subproblems.title: Area formula with fibre-sum measurability for locally Lipschitz maps on open subsets of ℝⁿ

With Ju(x) := √det(⟨Du(x)e_i, Du(x)e_j⟩)_{i,j}, Du(x) = fderiv ℝ u x, the fibre sum N(y) := Σ_{x ∈ D, u(x) = y} w(x) is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable on ℝ^Q and ∫_D w(x)·Ju(x) dLⁿ(x) = ∫_{ℝ^Q} N dHⁿ.

It is fact (F10) of the sibling pushforward_homotopy. There it proves the product formula H^{k+1}⌞((0,1)×M) = L¹ × H^k⌞M behind A4(d) (Simon 3.2(2), 'the area formula for the C¹ product manifold' in the supplied proof), applied to (s, v) ↦ (s, F_j(v)) and to F_j with weights 1/multiplicity on bounded pieces. Its own dependency fiber_sum_glue is reused alongside it. The accepted, independently audited natural-language proof of this exact statement follows verbatim.

Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure); Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i : Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ. For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k, JT := √det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Gram-determinant Jacobian); for a map φ, Jφ(w) := J(fderiv ℝ φ w). For B ⊆ X, a map f and a weight h ≥ 0, the fibre sum is N_B(y) := Σ_{x ∈ B, f(x) = y} h(x), the unordered sum in [0,∞] (∑' over the subtype {x // x ∈ B ∧ f x = y}). c-antilipschitz on Ω means c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is step 5 of the parent proof (area formula for u_j = f∘Φ_j with measurability, via a countable cover by balls on which u_j is Lipschitz) for a general locally Lipschitz u; it is also the engine of step 4. Add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaDomain` to the Submission header (or to a new file under GMT/Ch06/ that the Submission imports); it transitively imports Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.NormDet, so LinearMap.normDet and Matrix.gram become available. Adding this import was checked to leave all Contract definitions and all frozen statement types unchanged (the comparator only byte-checks the Contract and Lake files). Do not re-prove the Euclidean area formula: use the SimonGMT theorems cited below.

1. (Jacobian normalization.) For every linear T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q, normDet(T) = JT. Indeed (e_i) is the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply: its i-th vector is EuclideanSpace.single i 1), so LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram gives normDet(T)² = det(Matrix.gram ℝ (T e_·)) = det(⟨T e_i, T e_j⟩)_{i,j} (Matrix.gram is Matrix.of fun i j => ⟪v i, v j⟫); since normDet(T) ≥ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg), normDet(T) = √(normDet(T)²) = JT.
2. (Countable Lipschitz cover.) For each x ∈ Ω, local Lipschitzness gives K_x ≥ 0 and t_x ∈ 𝓝[Ω] x with u K_x-Lipschitz on t_x; as Ω is open, 𝓝[Ω] x = 𝓝 x (IsOpen.nhdsWithin_eq), so there is r_x > 0 with ball(x, r_x) ⊆ t_x ∩ Ω. These balls cover Ω and ℝⁿ is second countable, so a countable S ⊆ Ω satisfies Ω ⊆ ⋃_{x ∈ S} ball(x, r_x) (TopologicalSpace.countable_cover_nhdsWithin). If S = ∅ then Ω = ∅ and D = ∅: every fibre is empty, N ≡ 0 (measurable) and both integrals vanish. Otherwise write S = {s_0, s_1, …} (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range) and put V_m := ball(s_m, r_{s_m}): V_m is open, V_m ⊆ Ω, u is K_m-Lipschitz on V_m (K_m := K_{s_m}), and Ω ⊆ ⋃_m V_m.
3. (Disjoint pieces.) Let V′_m := V_m ∖ ⋃_{l<m} V_l (disjointed V): Borel, pairwise disjoint, V′_m ⊆ V_m and ⋃_m V′_m = ⋃_m V_m (iUnion_disjointed). Put D_m := D ∩ V′_m. Then D_m ⊆ D, D_m ⊆ V_m, the D_m are pairwise disjoint, each D_m is Lⁿ-null-measurable, and D ⊆ ⋃_m D_m because D ⊆ Ω ⊆ ⋃_m V′_m.
4. (Area formula on one piece.) Fix m. u is K_m-Lipschitz on D_m ⊆ V_m, D_m is null-measurable, and w is a.e.-measurable for Lⁿ⌞D_m (AEMeasurable.mono_set, D_m ⊆ D). The weighted area formula for Lipschitz maps on measurable subsets of ℝⁿ (Simon Ch. 2 (3.5); SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum with E = ℝⁿ, F = ℝ^Q, finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n by finrank_euclideanSpace_fin) and its measurability companion (aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn) state that N_m(y) := Σ_{x ∈ D_m, u(x) = y} w(x) (which is weightedAreaFiberSum D_m u w y by definition) is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable and ∫ N_m dHⁿ = ∫_{D_m} normDet(fderivWithin ℝ u D_m x)·w(x) dLⁿ(x) (the integrand is ENNReal.ofReal (areaJacobianWithin u D_m x) * w x).
5. (Within-derivative versus derivative.) Let g_m be a global Lipschitz extension of u|V_m (exists_lipschitz_extension_finiteDimensional), so u = g_m on V_m. By ae_fderivWithin_eq_of_lipschitz_extension (applied to D_m, with u = g_m on D_m), fderivWithin ℝ u D_m x = fderiv ℝ g_m x for Lⁿ⌞D_m-a.e. x. For x ∈ D_m ⊆ V_m, u and g_m agree on the open neighbourhood V_m of x, so fderiv ℝ u x = fderiv ℝ g_m x (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Hence for Lⁿ⌞D_m-a.e. x, normDet(fderivWithin ℝ u D_m x) = normDet(fderiv ℝ u x) = Ju(x) by step 1, and therefore ∫_{D_m} w·Ju dLⁿ = ∫ N_m dHⁿ (lintegral_congr_ae and commutativity of multiplication).
6. (Gluing.) Apply the sibling lemma fiber_sum_glue with X = ℝⁿ, μ = Lⁿ, Y = ℝ^Q, ν = Hⁿ, map u, weight h := w, integrand F(x) := w(x)·ofReal(Ju(x)), A := D, Z := ∅ and B := (D_m)_m: (a)–(c) and (d) D ⊆ ∅ ∪ ⋃_m D_m hold by step 3, (e) Lⁿ(∅) = 0, (f) Hⁿ(u(∅)) = Hⁿ(∅) = 0, and (g) holds by steps 4–5. Its conclusions are exactly the two claims. ∎
proof_key_steps: normDet T = √det Gram(T e_i) (LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram with EuclideanSpace.basisFun).
Countable cover of Ω by balls V_m ⊆ Ω on which u is Lipschitz (countable_cover_nhdsWithin); empty case trivial.
Disjoint null-measurable pieces D_m = D ∩ disjointed V m covering D.
SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum and aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn on each D_m.
fderivWithin u D_m = fderiv u a.e. on D_m via a Lipschitz extension (ae_fderivWithin_eq_of_lipschitz_extension, EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
Glue the pieces with fiber_sum_glue (Z = ∅).

subproblems.title: The lattice n-skeleton ⋃_F latticeFace ρ F is closed
subproblems.statement: For all n, N ∈ ℕ and ρ > 0, the union over all face indices F ∈ LatticeFaceIndex n N of the closed lattice faces latticeFace ρ F (the n-skeleton of the cubical decomposition of ℝ^N of side ρ) is a closed subset of ℝ^N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → IsClosed (⋃ F : LatticeFaceIndex n N, latticeFace ρ F)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 of the supplied proof of deformation_onto_skeleton ("ψ maps ℝ^d ∖ La into the closed set L_n"; Simon Ch. 6, §5, printed (22)), where the closedness of the n-skeleton L_n = ⋃_F latticeFace 1 F is used to pass from spt ψ_#X_ν ⊆ closure ψ(spt X_ν) to spt ψ_#X_ν ⊆ L_n. Here it is proved for an arbitrary lattice size ρ > 0 and arbitrary dimensions n, N.

Notation. For F = (z, α) ∈ LatticeFaceIndex n N = (Fin N → ℤ) × SimonMultiIndex n N (α : Fin n ↪o Fin N strictly increasing), latticeFace ρ F = {x ∈ ℝ^N : ∀ i, (i ∈ range α → ρz_i ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1)) ∧ (i ∉ range α → x_i = ρz_i)}. For x ∈ ℝ^N, x_i is its i-th coordinate; |x_i − y_i| ≤ |x − y| (Euclidean norm).

1. (Each face is closed.) Fix F = (z, α). For each i ∈ Fin N let S_i := {x : ρz_i ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1)} if i ∈ range α and S_i := {x : x_i = ρz_i} if i ∉ range α. The coordinate map x ↦ x_i is continuous (a continuous linear functional), so S_i is closed (preimage of a closed interval, resp. of a point; IsClosed.inter of isClosed_le, resp. isClosed_eq). For every x, the i-th conjunct of the defining predicate of latticeFace ρ F holds iff x ∈ S_i (case split on i ∈ range α). Hence latticeFace ρ F = ⋂_i S_i is closed (isClosed_iInter).

2. (Coordinates of points of a face.) If y ∈ latticeFace ρ (z, α) then ρz_i ≤ y_i ≤ ρz_i + ρ for every i: for i ∈ range α this is the first conjunct, and for i ∉ range α we have y_i = ρz_i. In particular |y_i − ρz_i| ≤ ρ for all i.

3. (Local finiteness.) Let x ∈ ℝ^N and W := ball(x, ρ), an open neighbourhood of x. Suppose W meets latticeFace ρ (z, α) at a point y. Then for every i, by Step 2, |x_i − ρz_i| ≤ |x_i − y_i| + |y_i − ρz_i| < ρ + ρ = 2ρ, i.e. z_i lies in the bounded real interval (x_i/ρ − 2, x_i/ρ + 2) (here ρ > 0 is used). Each such interval contains at most finitely many integers (at most 4), so the set Z_x of all z ∈ ℤ^N with |x_i − ρz_i| < 2ρ for all i is finite (it is contained in the finite product ∏_i of finite sets of integers). The type SimonMultiIndex n N is finite: an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin N is determined by its underlying function Fin n → Fin N (injectivity of the coercion), and the function type Fin n → Fin N is finite (Finite.of_injective). Hence the set of indices F with latticeFace ρ F ∩ W ≠ ∅ is contained in the finite set Z_x × SimonMultiIndex n N. This is exactly the statement that the family (latticeFace ρ F)_F is locally finite.

4. (Conclusion.) A locally finite union of closed sets is closed (LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion). By Steps 1 and 3, ⋃_F latticeFace ρ F is closed. (If n > N there are no strictly increasing α : Fin n → Fin N, the union is empty and the claim is trivial; the argument above covers this case as well.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Each latticeFace ρ F is an intersection over coordinates of closed slabs or hyperplanes, hence closed.
A ball of radius ρ around x meets latticeFace ρ (z, α) only if |x_i − ρz_i| < 2ρ for all i: finitely many z, and SimonMultiIndex n N is finite, so the family is locally finite.
A locally finite union of closed sets is closed.

subproblems.title: Chebyshev choice of a good slicing radius (parent Step 2, printed (10))
subproblems.statement: Let a < b be real, g : ℝ → [0, ∞] measurable with ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g ≤ K (K ∈ [0, ∞]) and N ⊆ ℝ Lebesgue-null. Then there is t ∈ (a, b) with t ∉ N and g(t) ≤ 2K/(b − a).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (a b : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (K : ℝ≥0∞) (N : Set ℝ), a < b → Measurable g → ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g t ≤ K → volume N = 0 → ∃ t ∈ Ioo a b, t ∉ N ∧ g t ≤ 2 * K / ENNReal.ofReal (b - a)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the supplied proof of deformation_onto_skeleton ("Good radii", printed (10)): "with g the majorant on (2^{−ν−1}, 2^{−ν}) …, Chebyshev's inequality shows that the set of t where g(t) is large has measure less than a fixed fraction of the interval, while the other two conditions fail only on null sets". This child isolates that selection in the form used there: the null set N collects the radii to be avoided (where the slice of ∂T has infinite mass and, optionally, where the slice of T fails to be integer multiplicity).

Notation. Lebesgue measure on ℝ is volume; I := Ioo a b; ℓ := ENNReal.ofReal(b − a). Since a < b, 0 < ℓ < ∞ and volume(I) = ℓ (Real.volume_Ioo). Put s := 2·K/ℓ ∈ [0, ∞] and B := {t ∈ I : s < g(t)}. All arithmetic is in [0, ∞].

1. (Claim: volume(B) < ℓ.) Three cases.
   (a) K = ∞. Then s = 2·∞/ℓ = ∞ because ℓ ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.div_eq_top). No value of g exceeds ∞, so B = ∅ and volume(B) = 0 < ℓ.
   (b) K = 0. Then ∫⁻_I g = 0, and since g is measurable, g = 0 almost everywhere on I with respect to volume.restrict I (lintegral_eq_zero_iff). Here s = 0 and B = I ∩ {g > 0} = I ∩ {g ≠ 0}, so volume(B) = volume.restrict I {g ≠ 0} = 0 < ℓ.
   (c) 0 < K < ∞. Then 0 < s < ∞. Markov's inequality for the measure volume.restrict I (mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral, g measurable) gives s · volume(I ∩ {g ≥ s}) ≤ ∫⁻_I g ≤ K. Dividing by s ∈ (0, ∞): volume(I ∩ {g ≥ s}) ≤ K/s = K·ℓ/(2K) = ℓ/2. Since B ⊆ I ∩ {g ≥ s}, volume(B) ≤ ℓ/2 < ℓ (ℓ ∈ (0, ∞)).

2. (Choice of t.) Suppose, for contradiction, that every t ∈ I lies in B ∪ N. Then I ⊆ B ∪ N, so ℓ = volume(I) ≤ volume(B) + volume(N) = volume(B) < ℓ (measure_union_le, monotonicity, volume N = 0), a contradiction. Hence there is t ∈ I with t ∉ B and t ∉ N.

3. (Conclusion.) For this t we have t ∈ Ioo a b, t ∉ N, and t ∉ B means ¬(s < g(t)), i.e. g(t) ≤ s = 2·K/ENNReal.ofReal(b − a). ∎

Remark (how the parent uses it). In Step 2 of the parent, g is the measurable majorant supplied by the SlicingTheorem on the interval (2^{−ν−1}, 2^{−ν}) for T and f = d_a (L_W = 1, W = ℝ^d), with K = M(T⌞{2^{−ν−1} < d_a < 2^{−ν}}) ≤ c_B 2^{−ν(n+1)} M(T); then g(σ_ν) ≤ 2K/2^{−ν−1} = 2^{ν+2}K ≤ 4c_B 2^{−νn} M(T), which is (10) (even with 4 in place of 8). The null set N is: when n ≥ 2, Ioo(2^{−ν−1}, 2^{−ν}) ∩ {t : g′(t) = ∞}, where g′ is the slicing majorant for ∂T on that interval (null because ∫ g′ < ∞), so that M(S′_{σ_ν}) ≤ g′(σ_ν) < ∞; when T is integer multiplicity one may add the null set {t : S_t is not integer multiplicity} to reproduce the printed requirement that S_{σ_ν} be integer multiplicity (not needed for the conclusions, since the integrality of Q, R, S comes from the pieces X_ν, Z′_ν); when n = 1 and T is not integer multiplicity, N = ∅.
proof_key_steps: Put s := 2K/(b − a) and B := {t ∈ (a,b) : g(t) > s}.
volume(B) < b − a: trivially if K = ∞; by g = 0 a.e. if K = 0; by Markov (volume ≤ K/s = (b − a)/2) if 0 < K < ∞.
If (a,b) ⊆ B ∪ N then b − a ≤ volume(B) + volume(N) < b − a; so some t ∈ (a,b) avoids B ∪ N, and g(t) ≤ s.

The parent applies these tools to the single map f = ψ of deformation_retraction on the regions E = {d_a ≥ σ}; here they are stated for an arbitrary map f : ℝ^D → ℝ^D on an arbitrary closed region E on whose δ-neighbourhood f is Lipschitz. Using one map f for all regions replaces the parent's σ-dependent extensions ψ̄_σ, h̄_σ: the operators below depend only on f, and their independence of the region is proved in Step 6.2 exactly as the parent's I.6 proves independence of σ (via the support clause of 2.28). PART 0 — NOTATION AND STANDING FACTS.

0.1 (Notation.) For m ∈ ℕ, ℝ^m = Eucl m with standard basis e_1,…,e_m (indexed by Fin m) and Euclidean norm |·|. D_k(ℝ^m) := GeometricCurrentOn univ k, D^k(ℝ^m) := TestFormOn univ k. For a k-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{γ∈I(k,m)} α(e_γ)²)^{1/2}; for a k-form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| (finite for continuous compactly supported ω). M = mass, M_W = massOn W, spt = support. ‖A‖ is the operator norm of a linear map. For a C¹ map g : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} and a k-form ω on ℝ^{m′}, g^#ω(x) := (ω(g(x))).compContinuousLinearMap(Dg(x)), i.e. g^#ω(x)(v_1,…,v_k) = ω(g(x))(Dg(x)v_1,…,Dg(x)v_k). For A ⊆ ℝ^m and r > 0, A_r := thickening r A = {x : dist(x, A) < r} (open; mem_thickening_iff: x ∈ A_r iff some a ∈ A has |x − a| < r; ∅_r = ∅). A current X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) is called normal if M(X) < ∞ and, when k = j + 1, M(∂X) < ∞. (In the Lean statement the boundary condition for a general degree k is written "for every j and Y ∈ D_{j+1} with k = j + 1 and HEq Y X, M(∂Y) < ∞"; for k = 0 it is vacuous, and for k = j + 1 it is equivalent to M(∂X) < ∞, by specializing to Y := X, resp. by Nat.succ.inj and eq_of_heq.)

0.2 (Reused facts; sibling children. (F1)–(F3), (F9), (F10) are reused comparator-accepted declarations declared as dependencies of this child; (F4) is a SimonGMT theorem; (F5)–(F8), (F11) are proved here.)
 (F1) mass_bound: if 0 ≤ B′, M_W(Y) ≤ B′, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ C′ for all x, then |Y(ω)| ≤ B′C′. In particular |Y(ω)| ≤ M(Y)‖ω‖ when M(Y) < ∞.
 (F2) vanish_off_support: Y(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ spt Y = ∅.
 (F2′) Consequence: if η, η′ ∈ D^k agree on an open set N ⊇ spt Y, then Y(η) = Y(η′). Indeed η − η′ vanishes on N, so tsupport(η − η′) ⊆ closure(ℝ^m ∖ N) = ℝ^m ∖ N (N open), which is disjoint from spt Y; apply (F2) and linearity. Also: a current with empty support is 0 (apply (F2) to every ω).
 (F3) support_lemmas: (1) spt ∂Y ⊆ spt Y; (2) weak limits of currents supported in a closed set F are supported in F; (3) spt(aY₁ + bY₂) ⊆ spt Y₁ ∪ spt Y₂ (for a current equal pointwise to aY₁ + bY₂).
 (F4) Lower semicontinuity (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf): if Y_j ⇀ Y then M(Y) ≤ liminf_j M(Y_j).
 (F5) If TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 then ‖ω_j‖ → 0 and ‖dω_j‖ → 0: all supports lie in one compact K, iteratedFDeriv ℝ q ω_j → 0 uniformly on K for q = 0, 1; ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ and dω_j(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dω_j(x)) has operator norm ≤ (k+1)‖Dω_j(x)‖; finally |α| ≤ √(m^k)·‖α‖ for every k-covector (each coefficient α(e_γ) has absolute value ≤ ‖α‖).
 (F6) Criterion: if T : D^k(ℝ^m) → ℝ is linear and |T(ω)| ≤ B‖ω‖ for all ω, then T is a current (sequential continuity by (F5)). More generally it suffices that for every compact K there is B_K with |T(ω)| ≤ B_K‖ω‖ for all ω with tsupport ω ⊆ K.
 (F7) Pull-back bound: for a linear A : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} and a k-covector α on ℝ^{m′}, |α∘A| ≤ ‖A‖^k|α|, where (α∘A)(v) := α(Av_1,…,Av_k). Proof: for an alternating k-form γ on ℝ^p, Σ_{I∈[p]^k} γ(e_{I_1},…,e_{I_k})² = k!·|γ|² (tuples with a repeated index contribute 0; each increasing γ-tuple arises from k! orderings, with the same square). One-slot bound: for a linear functional λ on ℝ^{m′}, Σ_{a} λ(Ae_a)² = |Aᵀλ|² ≤ ‖A‖²|λ|² = ‖A‖² Σ_b λ(e_b)². Applying the one-slot bound successively to slots 1,…,k (the other slots fixed) gives Σ_{I∈[m]^k} α(Ae_{I_1},…,Ae_{I_k})² ≤ ‖A‖^{2k} Σ_{J∈[m′]^k} α(e_{J_1},…,e_{J_k})², i.e. k!|α∘A|² ≤ ‖A‖^{2k}k!|α|². (The same computation is carried out in the accepted declarations iwl_sp_pn_sum_sq_comp_basis_le and iwl_sp_pn_multilinear_sum_sq_le of another branch, which a later decomposition of this child may reuse; the argument given here is complete.)
 (F8) Interior product: for a (k+1)-covector α on ℝ^{m′} and w ∈ ℝ^{m′}, the k-covector α(w, ·) satisfies |α(w, ·)| ≤ c₁|w||α| with c₁ = c₁(m′, k) := √(m′^k)·√m′: indeed α(w, e_γ) = Σ_i w_i α(e_i, e_γ) and each α(e_i, e_γ) is ± a coefficient of α or 0, so |α(w, e_γ)| ≤ √m′|w||α|. Consequently, for linear A : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, the k-covector v ↦ α(w, Av_1,…,Av_k) has norm ≤ c₁|w|‖A‖^k|α| (by (F7) applied to α(w, ·)).

Expand each τ_i = Σ_a τ_i^a e_a: α(τ) = Σ_{J∈[p]^k} (Π_i τ_i^{J_i}) α(e_{J_1},…,e_{J_k}); each |α(e_J)| ≤ |α| (it is ± a coefficient of α or 0), and Σ_J Π_i|τ_i^{J_i}| = Π_i Σ_a|τ_i^a| ≤ (√p)^k.

PART 1 — LIPSCHITZ MAPS: EXTENSION AND MOLLIFICATION.

1.1 (McShane extension.) If F : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} is Λ-Lipschitz on a set A, there is F̂ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, √m′·Λ-Lipschitz on ℝ^m, with F̂ = F on A: each coordinate F_i is Λ-Lipschitz on A (|F_i(x) − F_i(y)| ≤ |F(x) − F(y)|), extend it by LipschitzOnWith.extend_real to a Λ-Lipschitz F̂_i on ℝ^m, and put F̂ := (F̂_i)_i; then |F̂(x) − F̂(y)|² = Σ_i|F̂_i(x) − F̂_i(y)|² ≤ m′Λ²|x − y|².

1.2 (Mollifier.) Fix a C^∞ function ϕ ≥ 0 on ℝ^m with tsupport ϕ ⊆ closedBall(0, 1/2) and ∫ϕ = 1 (take a smooth bump b ≥ 0 with b(0) = 1 and tsupport b ⊆ closedBall(0, 1/2) from exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset, and normalize by ∫b > 0). For σ > 0 put ϕ_σ(w) := σ^{−m}ϕ(w/σ): C^∞, ≥ 0, support in the open ball B_σ(0), ∫ϕ_σ = 1. For a continuous G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} put G_σ(x) := ∫ G(x − w)ϕ_σ(w)dw (the convolution of ϕ_σ with G for the scalar action).
 (a) G_σ is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left: ϕ_σ is C^∞ with compact support and G is locally integrable).
 (b) (Locality.) G_σ(x) only depends on G restricted to B_σ(x) (the integrand vanishes for |w| ≥ σ). In particular: if G = G′ on B_σ(x) then G_σ(x) = G′_σ(x); if the i-th coordinate G_i equals a constant c on B_σ(x), then (G_σ)_i(x) = c (∫ϕ_σ = 1).

Then η_s = j_s^#η and, by the chain rule D(G∘j_s)(x) = DG(s, x)∘ι, j_s^#(G^#ω) = (F_s)^#ω; so η_s is compatible with (F_s, ω) near spt X (on j_s⁻¹(Ñ) ⊇ spt X), and G_#({s}×X)(ω) = ({s}×X)(η) = X(η_s) = (F_s)_#X(ω).
4.2 (Homotopy formula; Simon 2.25.) For k = j + 1: (F_1)_#X − (F_0)_#X = ∂G_#Z + G_#([[0,1]]×∂X); for k = 0: (F_1)_#X − (F_0)_#X = ∂G_#Z. Proof: all supports involved lie in [0,1] × spt X, on which G is proper; by 2.5, 2.2 (linearity) and 3.4, ∂G_#Z = G_#∂Z = G_#({1}×X) − G_#({0}×X) − G_#([[0,1]]×∂X), and 4.1 identifies the first two terms.
4.3 (Affine estimate; Simon 2.27.) Suppose moreover G(t, x) = F_0(x) + t(F_1(x) − F_0(x)) and O ⊇ spt X is an open set with |F_1 − F_0| ≤ s and ‖DF_0‖, ‖DF_1‖ ≤ L on O. Then for every ψ ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m′}): |G_#Z(ψ)| ≤ c₁(m′, k)·s·L^k·M(X)·‖ψ‖. Proof: G^#ψ(t, x)(e_0, ιv_1,…,ιv_k) = ψ(G(t, x))(F_1(x) − F_0(x), A_t(x)v_1,…,A_t(x)v_k) with A_t := (1 − t)DF_0 + tDF_1, ‖A_t‖ ≤ L on O for t ∈ [0,1]. Choose η̃ = ζ̃·G^#ψ compatible with (G, ψ) near [0,1] × spt X with tsupport ζ̃ ⊆ ℝ × O (2.1 with the open set ℝ × O ⊇ C̃). For t ∈ [0,1]: η̃^{(t)}(x) = 0 if x ∉ O, and otherwise |η̃^{(t)}(x)| ≤ c₁|F_1(x) − F_0(x)|‖A_t(x)‖^k|ψ(G(t, x))| ≤ c₁sL^k‖ψ‖ by (F8). So |G_#Z(ψ)| = |∫_0^1 X(η̃^{(t)}) dt| ≤ M(X)·c₁sL^k‖ψ‖ (F1).
4.4 (Consequence; Simon 2.28.) Under 4.3, for ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}): |(F_1)_#X(ω) − (F_0)_#X(ω)| ≤ c₁(m′, k)·s·L^k·M(X)·‖dω‖ + c₁(m′, k−1)·s·L^{k−1}·M(∂X)·‖ω‖ (the second term only for k ≥ 1). Indeed by 4.2, (F_1)_#X(ω) − (F_0)_#X(ω) = G_#Z(dω) + G_#([[0,1]]×∂X)(ω), and 4.3 applies to X with the form dω and to ∂X (degree k − 1, finite mass, spt ∂X ⊆ spt X) with the form ω.
PART 5 — PUSH-FORWARD BY LIPSCHITZ MAPS (Simon 2.28–2.29; parent A2(e), I.7).
Let X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) be normal and G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} globally L-Lipschitz with G|spt X proper. If (G_j) is an admissible approximating sequence (Part 1) with constant L′, then for j large (sup|G_j − G| ≤ 1) G_j|spt X is proper (G_j⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X ⊆ G⁻¹(cthickening 1 K) ∩ spt X, a closed subset of a compact set), so (G_j)_#X is defined (Part 2), and by 2.3(ii) with O = ℝ^m, |(G_j)_#X(ω)| ≤ L′^kM(X)‖ω‖.

5.1 (Existence and independence of the limit; Simon 2.29.) For every admissible approximating sequence (G_j) and every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}), lim_j (G_j)_#X(ω) exists, and it is the same for all admissible approximating sequences of G. Proof. For i, j large let G_{ij}(t, x) := G_i(x) + t(G_j(x) − G_i(x)); it is C^∞ and proper on [0,1] × spt X (|G_{ij}(t, x) − G(x)| ≤ 1 there). Apply 4.4 with O = ℝ^m, L = L′, s = sup|G_i − G_j|: |(G_j)_#X(ω) − (G_i)_#X(ω)| ≤ sup|G_i − G_j|·(c₁L′^kM(X)‖dω‖ + c₁′L′^{k−1}M(∂X)‖ω‖) → 0 as i, j → ∞. So the real sequence is Cauchy and converges. If (G′_j) is a second admissible approximating sequence, the interleaved sequence G_1, G′_1, G_2, G′_2, … is admissible (common constant max(L′, L″)), so its limit exists and equals both subsequential limits.
 Definition: G_#X(ω) := lim_j (G_j)_#X(ω) (any admissible approximating sequence; e.g. the mollifications G_{1/j}).
5.2 (Characterization.) By definition and 2.2: for every admissible approximating sequence (G_j) and every choice of η_j compatible with (G_j, ω) near spt X, X(η_j) → G_#X(ω).
5.3 (Current.) ω ↦ G_#X(ω) is linear (limit of linear maps) and |G_#X(ω)| ≤ L′^kM(X)‖ω‖ (take G_j = G_{1/j}, L′ = L), so G_#X ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) by (F6), and (G_{1/j})_#X ⇀ G_#X.
5.4 (Locality.) If G, G′ are globally Lipschitz, proper on spt X, and G = G′ on (spt X)_r for some r > 0, then G_#X = G′_#X. Proof: for σ < r/2, the mollifications satisfy G_σ = G′_σ on the open set (spt X)_{r/2} (1.2(b): B_σ(x) ⊆ (spt X)_r for x ∈ (spt X)_{r/2}); a form compatible with (G_σ, ω) on N is compatible with (G′_σ, ω) on N ∩ (spt X)_{r/2} ⊇ spt X; so (G_σ)_#X = (G′_σ)_#X, and the limits agree.
5.5 (Mass with a local Lipschitz constant; Simon 2.29.) If G is Λ-Lipschitz on (spt X)_r for some r > 0, then M(G_#X) ≤ Λ^kM(X). Proof: for σ < r/4 and x ∈ O := (spt X)_{r/2}, B_{2σ}(x) ⊆ (spt X)_r, so ‖DG_σ(x)‖ ≤ Λ by 1.2(c); by 2.3(ii), M((G_σ)_#X) ≤ Λ^kM(X); and (G_σ)_#X ⇀ G_#X (5.3 with σ = 1/j), so (F4) gives M(G_#X) ≤ Λ^kM(X).
5.6 (Support.) spt G_#X ⊆ closure G(spt X). If tsupport ω misses closure G(spt X), then ρ₀ := dist(tsupport ω, G(spt X)) > 0 (compact versus closed, disjoint); for j with sup|G_j − G| < ρ₀, G_j(spt X) ∩ tsupport ω = ∅, so (G_j)_#X(ω) = 0 as in 2.4, hence G_#X(ω) = 0; conclude as in 2.4.
5.7 (Boundary.) If k = j + 1 then ∂(G_#X) = G_#(∂X) (∂X is normal: M(∂X) < ∞ and ∂∂X = 0; G is proper on spt ∂X ⊆ spt X). Indeed ∂(G_#X)(φ) = G_#X(dφ) = lim_j (G_j)_#X(dφ) = lim_j (G_j)_#(∂X)(φ) = G_#(∂X)(φ) by 2.5.
5.8 (Linearity in X.) If X, X′ are normal, G is proper on spt X ∪ spt X′ and X″ = aX + a′X′ pointwise (X″ is then normal), then G_#X″ = aG_#X + a′G_#X′, by 2.2 and passage to the limit.
5.9 (Integrality; parent I.7.) If moreover X is integer multiplicity, X = τ(M, θ, ξ) with IsRectifiableTriple univ k M θ ξ and θ(M) ⊆ ℕ, then G_#X is integer multiplicity. Proof: apply the premise (S5′) to X, (M, θ, ξ), g := G, Λ := L (G is L-Lipschitz, and G⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X is compact for compact K): there is an integer multiplicity S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) such that for every sequence of C¹ maps with a common Lipschitz bound converging uniformly to G and every ω, ∫_M θ(x)·nVectorPushforward k (Dg_j(x)) (ξ(x)) (ω(g_j(x))) dH^k(x) → S(ω). Take g_j := G_{1/j} (C^∞ ⊆ C¹, L-Lipschitz, uniformly convergent). By 2.6, (G_{1/j})_#X(ω) equals that integral; by 5.3 it converges to G_#X(ω). Hence G_#X(ω) = S(ω) for all ω, G_#X = S (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and G_#X is integer multiplicity.

PART 6 — THE OPERATORS P_k, H_k AND THE NINE CLAUSES (parent I.6, I.7, Step 7).
Fix D and put c_k := max{1, c₁(D, k)} (c₁ from (F8)); c_k depends only on (D, k). Fix f : ℝ^D → ℝ^D. Write E_δ = thickening δ E. Data (E, Λ, δ, b) are admissible for X ∈ D_k(ℝ^D) if E is closed, δ > 0, f is Λ-Lipschitz on E_δ, |f(x) − x| ≤ b for x ∈ E, X is normal and spt X ⊆ E. For such data put b₊ := max(b, 0) and b′ := b₊ + (1 + Λ)δ ≥ 0; then |x − f(x)| ≤ b′ on E_δ (if E_δ ≠ ∅, pick y ∈ E with |x − y| < δ; both x, y ∈ E_δ, so |x − f(x)| ≤ |x − y| + |y − f(y)| + |f(y) − f(x)| ≤ (1 + Λ)δ + b). (If E = ∅ then E_δ = ∅, X = 0 and everything below is trivial.) Define the straight-line homotopy from f to the identity, h(t, x) := f(x) + t(x − f(x)) (h(0, ·) = f, h(1, ·) = id). On Ã_E := [−1, 2] × E_δ ⊆ ℝ^{1+D}, h is L_h-Lipschitz with L_h := 3Λ + 2 + b′: h(t,x) − h(t′,x′) = (f(x) − f(x′)) + t[(x − x′) − (f(x) − f(x′))] + (t − t′)(x′ − f(x′)), so |h(t,x) − h(t′,x′)| ≤ (Λ + 2(1 + Λ))|x − x′| + b′|t − t′|.
 Choices: f̂_E := a √D·Λ-Lipschitz extension of f|E_δ to ℝ^D, and ĥ_E := a √D·L_h-Lipschitz extension of h|Ã_E to ℝ^{1+D} (1.1). Properness: on spt X ⊆ E, f̂_E = f and |f(x) − x| ≤ b, so f̂_E⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X ⊆ cthickening b K ∩ spt X is compact; on [0,1] × spt X, ĥ_E = h and |h(t, x) − x| = (1 − t)|f(x) − x| ≤ b, so ĥ_E⁻¹(K) ∩ ([0,1] × spt X) ⊆ [0,1] × (cthickening b K ∩ spt X) is compact.

6.1 (Definition.) If X ∈ D_k(ℝ^D) admits admissible data (E, Λ, δ, b), put P_kX := (f̂_E)_#X and H_kX := (ĥ_E)_#([[0,1]]×X) (Part 5; [[0,1]]×X is normal by 3.2, 3.4, with spt ⊆ [0,1] × spt X by 3.3, so ĥ_E is proper on its support). Otherwise put P_kX := 0, H_kX := 0. (Classical choice of data and extensions.)
6.2 (Independence of the choices; the parent's "independence of σ".) If (E, Λ, δ, b), (E′, Λ′, δ′, b″) are two admissible data for X, with extensions f̂_E, f̂_{E′}, ĥ_E, ĥ_{E′}, then f̂_E = f = f̂_{E′} on E_δ ∩ E′_{δ′} ⊇ (spt X)_{r} with r := min(δ, δ′), so (f̂_E)_#X = (f̂_{E′})_#X by 5.4; and ĥ_E = h = ĥ_{E′} on Ã_E ∩ Ã_{E′} ⊇ ([0,1] × spt X)_{r′} with r′ := min(1, δ, δ′) (a point within r′ of (t₀, x₀) ∈ [0,1] × spt X has t ∈ (−1, 2) and x ∈ (spt X)_{r′}), so (ĥ_E)_#([[0,1]]×X) = (ĥ_{E′})_#([[0,1]]×X) by 5.4 (in ℝ^{1+D}). Hence P_kX, H_kX do not depend on the choices, and for any admissible data they may be computed with f̂_E, ĥ_E. If spt X = ∅ then X = 0 (F2′) and P_kX = H_kX = 0.
Now fix X ∈ D_k(ℝ^D) with admissible data (E, Λ, δ, b) (this is exactly the hypothesis list of the first clause of the Lean statement, by 0.1).
6.3 (Clause (1), mass of P.) f̂_E = f is Λ-Lipschitz on (spt X)_δ ⊆ E_δ, so by 5.5, M(P_kX) ≤ Λ^kM(X) ≤ c_kΛ^kM(X).
6.4 (Clause (2), mass of H; Simon 2.27, parent (13), (14), (16).) If spt X = ∅ both sides vanish. Otherwise b ≥ 0. Let ĥ := ĥ_E and ĥ_σ its mollifications (on ℝ^{1+D}); they form an admissible approximating sequence of ĥ (σ = 1/j), so (ĥ_σ)_#Z ⇀ H_kX with Z := [[0,1]]×X (5.3), and M(H_kX) ≤ liminf_σ M((ĥ_σ)_#Z) (F4). Fix ε₁ ∈ (0, min(1, δ)/4) and σ < ε₁. For t ∈ [0,1] and x ∈ (spt X)_{ε₁}, the ball B_{2σ}((t, x)) lies in (−1, 2) × (spt X)_{3ε₁} ⊆ Ã_E (3ε₁ < δ), where ĥ = h. Since h is affine in t, ĥ_σ(t + τ, x) − ĥ_σ(t, x) = τ∫(x − w_x − f(x − w_x))ϕ_σ(w)dw for small τ, so ∂_tĥ_σ(t, x) = ∫(x − w_x − f(x − w_x))ϕ_σ(w)dw and |∂_tĥ_σ(t, x)| ≤ sup_{x′∈B_σ(x)}|x′ − f(x′)| ≤ b + (1 + Λ)·2ε₁ (each such x′ lies within ε₁ + σ < 2ε₁ of a point y ∈ spt X, where |y − f(y)| ≤ b, and x′, y ∈ E_δ, so |x′ − f(x′)| ≤ |y − f(y)| + (1 + Λ)|x′ − y|). For |t′ − t| < σ the map x′ ↦ h(t′, x′) = (1 − t′)f(x′) + t′x′ is (|1 − t′|Λ + |t′|)-Lipschitz on E_δ, hence x ↦ ĥ_σ(t, x) is (1 + σ)(1 + Λ)-Lipschitz near x and ‖D_xĥ_σ(t, x)‖ ≤ (1 + ε₁)(1 + Λ) (as in 1.2(c)). Let ψ ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^D) with ‖ψ‖ ≤ 1 and choose η̃ = ζ̃·ĥ_σ^#ψ compatible with (ĥ_σ, ψ) near [0,1] × spt X with tsupport ζ̃ ⊆ (−ε₁, 1 + ε₁) × (spt X)_{ε₁} (2.1). For t ∈ [0,1], η̃^{(t)}(x) = 0 unless x ∈ (spt X)_{ε₁}, and then, by (F8), |η̃^{(t)}(x)| ≤ |ψ(ĥ_σ(t, x))(∂_tĥ_σ(t, x), D_xĥ_σ(t, x)·)| ≤ c₁(b + 2(1 + Λ)ε₁)(1 + ε₁)^k(1 + Λ)^k. Hence |(ĥ_σ)_#Z(ψ)| = |∫_0^1 X(η̃^{(t)}) dt| ≤ c₁(b + 2(1 + Λ)ε₁)(1 + ε₁)^k(1 + Λ)^kM(X) for all σ < ε₁, so M(H_kX) ≤ c₁(b + 2(1 + Λ)ε₁)(1 + ε₁)^k(1 + Λ)^kM(X). Letting ε₁ ↓ 0: M(H_kX) ≤ c₁·b·(1 + Λ)^k·M(X) ≤ c_k·b·(1 + Λ)^k·M(X).
6.5 (Clause (3), support of P.) By 5.6, spt P_kX ⊆ closure f̂_E(spt X) = closure f(spt X).
6.6 (Clause (4), support of H.) By 5.6 and 3.3, spt H_kX ⊆ closure ĥ_E(spt Z) ⊆ closure h([0,1] × spt X); and |h(t, x) − x| = (1 − t)|f(x) − x| ≤ b for x ∈ spt X ⊆ E, so h([0,1] × spt X) ⊆ cthickening b (spt X), which is closed. (This is the convexity argument of the parent's Step 6.)
6.7 (Clause (5), integrality.) If X is integer multiplicity, P_kX = (f̂_E)_#X is integer multiplicity by 5.9. By 3.5, Z = [[0,1]]×X is integer multiplicity, and it is normal; hence H_kX = (ĥ_E)_#Z is integer multiplicity by 5.9 applied in ℝ^{1+D} → ℝ^D (the premise (S5′) is stated for all P, Q).
6.8 (Clause (6), tangential vanishing; the analytic core of the parent's Step 7.) Let α ∈ I(k, D), z ∈ ℝ^D, ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^D), ε > 0 satisfy: every x ∈ (spt X)_ε with f(x) ∈ (tsupport ω)_ε has f(x)_i = z_i for all i ∉ range α; and ω(y)(e_{α(1)},…,e_{α(k)}) = 0 for all y. Put r := min(ε, δ)/2, N := (spt X)_{r/2} (open, ⊇ spt X) and let σ < min(r/4, ε/(4Λ + 4)). Write F := f̂_E and F_σ for its mollification. Claim: F_σ^#ω = 0 on N. Let x ∈ N. If F_σ(x) ∉ tsupport ω then ω(F_σ(x)) = 0. Otherwise, for y ∈ B_{2σ}(x): y ∈ (spt X)_{r} ⊆ (spt X)_ε ∩ (spt X)_δ, so F(y) = f(y); B_{2σ}(x) ⊆ (spt X)_δ ⊆ E_δ, where f is Λ-Lipschitz, so |F_σ(x) − f(x)| ≤ Λσ (1.2(c)) and |f(y) − F_σ(x)| ≤ 2Λσ + Λσ < ε; thus f(y) ∈ (tsupport ω)_ε and, by hypothesis, f(y)_i = z_i for i ∉ range α. For x′ ∈ B_σ(x) and |w| < σ, x′ − w ∈ B_{2σ}(x), so (F_σ)_i(x′) = ∫ f(x′ − w)_i ϕ_σ(w)dw = z_i (1.2(b)). So for i ∉ range α the coordinate (F_σ)_i is constant on the open ball B_σ(x), D(F_σ)_i(x) = 0, and DF_σ(x) maps ℝ^D into V_α := span{e_{α(1)},…,e_{α(k)}}. An alternating k-form β with β(e_{α(1)},…,e_{α(k)}) = 0 vanishes on V_α^k (expand u_i = Σ_j c_{ij}e_{α(j)} multilinearly: terms with a repeated basis vector vanish and the others are ± β(e_{α(1)},…,e_{α(k)}) = 0, i.e. β(u) = det(c)·β(e_α)). Applying this to β := ω(F_σ(x)) and u_i := DF_σ(x)v_i gives F_σ^#ω(x) = 0. So the zero form is compatible with (F_σ, ω) near spt X, and (F_σ)_#X(ω) = X(0) = 0 for all small σ. By 5.2 (with the admissible approximating sequence F_{σ_j}, σ_j ↓ 0), P_kX(ω) = lim 0 = 0.
6.9 (Clause (7), linearity.) Let X₁ have the same admissible data (E, Λ, δ, b) and X₂(ω) = aX(ω) + a₁X₁(ω) for all ω. Then X₂ is normal (M(X₂) ≤ |a|M(X) + |a₁|M(X₁) by (F1) applied to mass-admissible forms; for k = j + 1, ∂X₂ = a∂X + a₁∂X₁ pointwise, so M(∂X₂) ≤ |a|M(∂X) + |a₁|M(∂X₁) < ∞) and spt X₂ ⊆ spt X ∪ spt X₁ ⊆ E (F3(3)); so (E, Λ, δ, b) is admissible for X₂ as well. Computing all three operators with the same f̂_E and ĥ_E (6.2): P_kX₂ = (f̂_E)_#X₂ = a(f̂_E)_#X + a₁(f̂_E)_#X₁ by 5.8; and [[0,1]]×X₂ = a[[0,1]]×X + a₁[[0,1]]×X₁ (3.2 is linear in X), so H_kX₂ = aH_kX + a₁H_kX₁ by 5.8 in ℝ^{1+D}.
6.10 (Clause (8), boundary.) Let k = j + 1 and X ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^D) with admissible data (M(X), M(∂X) < ∞, spt X ⊆ E). Then ∂X ∈ D_j has the same admissible data (M(∂X) < ∞; ∂∂X = 0 has mass 0 when j ≥ 1; spt ∂X ⊆ spt X ⊆ E by (F3)(1)). By 5.7 with G = f̂_E: ∂P_{j+1}X = ∂((f̂_E)_#X) = (f̂_E)_#(∂X) = P_j(∂X).
6.11 (Clause (9), homotopy formula; Simon 2.25 with f at t = 0 and the identity at t = 1, i.e. the parent's corrected (20).) Same X. Let ĥ := ĥ_E and ĥ_σ its mollifications (σ = 1/j), and Z := [[0,1]]×X. For σ ≤ 1, ĥ_σ is C^∞ and proper on [0,1] × spt X (|ĥ_σ − ĥ| ≤ √D L_hσ), so 4.2 applies to G := ĥ_σ: with F_s^σ := ĥ_σ∘j_s,
   (F_1^σ)_#X − (F_0^σ)_#X = ∂(ĥ_σ)_#Z + (ĥ_σ)_#([[0,1]]×∂X).
 Let σ → 0 and evaluate on a fixed ω ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^D). (i) (ĥ_σ)_#Z ⇀ ĥ_#Z = H_{j+1}X (5.3), so ∂(ĥ_σ)_#Z(ω) = (ĥ_σ)_#Z(dω) → H_{j+1}X(dω) = ∂H_{j+1}X(ω). (ii) [[0,1]]×∂X is normal with support in [0,1] × spt ∂X ⊆ [0,1] × spt X, and ∂X has the admissible data (E, Λ, δ, b) (6.10), so (ĥ_σ)_#([[0,1]]×∂X)(ω) → ĥ_#([[0,1]]×∂X)(ω) = H_j(∂X)(ω). (iii) F_s^σ is C^∞, √D L_h-Lipschitz and converges uniformly to ĥ∘j_s; hence (F_s^σ)_#X(ω) → (ĥ∘j_s)_#X(ω) (5.1). Now ĥ∘j_1 = h(1, ·) = id on E_δ ⊇ (spt X)_δ, and id_#X = X (the constant sequence id is admissible, and a form compatible with (id, ω) near spt X agrees with ω near spt X, so (F2′) gives id_#X(ω) = X(ω)); by 5.4, (ĥ∘j_1)_#X = X. Similarly ĥ∘j_0 = h(0, ·) = f = f̂_E on (spt X)_δ, so (ĥ∘j_0)_#X = (f̂_E)_#X = P_{j+1}X. Passing to the limit: X(ω) − P_{j+1}X(ω) = ∂H_{j+1}X(ω) + H_j(∂X)(ω) for every ω.
6.12 (Conclusion.)
